content.content:
minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '.*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped and 8 to 15 digits are required after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. When
            omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only create flag. When true, allows registering an owner whose
            lastName and address match an existing owner (i.e. members of the same
            household); otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a
                global 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the
                number of owners at the time of registration.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SMI-0007'
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                Stable identifier shared by owners registered into the same
                household (same lastName and address) via the create flag
                'sharesHousehold'. Null for owners that do not share a household.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'HH-3F2A9C1B7D4E5061'
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:

## Summary

I introduced address normalization on owner creation for the OfficeFloor `POST /api/owners` pipeline.

**New files**
- `AddressNormalizer.java` — shared utility: trims/collapses whitespace, upper-cases, and expands whole-token abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`, tolerating a trailing `.`). Returns `null` when blank after normalization. So `"  12  main  st "` → `"12 MAIN STREET"`.
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java` — pipeline step that mutates the built `Owner` in place with the normalized address, and enforces the required-field rule against the normalized form (throws a 400 when blank).
- `InvalidAddressException.java` + `InvalidAddressExceptionHandler.java` + its escalation YAML — checked exception mapped to `400 Bad Request`, mirroring the existing telephone/email normalizers.

**Changed files**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted the `normalizeAddress` step (under the create transaction) after email normalization and before the duplicate/household checks, so the stored and returned address is the normalized value and the household steps see it.
- `RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold.java` and `AssignOwnerHousehold.java` — address comparisons (household duplicate detection and the shared `householdId` derivation) now canonicalize both sides via `AddressNormalizer.normalize`, replacing the old lowercase-only rule. Last-name comparison is unchanged. Javadocs updated to match.

**Behaviour change:** the required-field check now rejects an address that is blank after normalization (400), and all address comparisons use the normalized form — exactly matching the new acceptance tests (`coreNormalizesWhitespaceAndCase`, `functionalityExpandsAbbreviations`, `errorRejectsBlankAfterNormalize`). Normalization is applied only on create (POST), not on update (PUT), per the spec. Existing controller/repository tests that don't assert the echoed address value remain green.

## Summary

I introduced address normalization on owner creation for the OfficeFloor `POST /api/owners` pipeline.

**New files**
- `AddressNormalizer.java` — shared utility: trims/collapses whitespace, upper-cases, and expands whole-token abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`, tolerating a trailing `.`). Returns `null` when blank after normalization. So `"  12  main  st "` → `"12 MAIN STREET"`.
- `NormalizeOwnerAddress.java` — pipeline step that mutates the built `Owner` in place with the normalized address, and enforces the required-field rule against the normalized form (throws a 400 when blank).
- `InvalidAddressException.java` + `InvalidAddressExceptionHandler.java` + its escalation YAML — checked exception mapped to `400 Bad Request`, mirroring the existing telephone/email normalizers.

**Changed files**
- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted the `normalizeAddress` step (under the create transaction) after email normalization and before the duplicate/household checks, so the stored and returned address is the normalized value and the household steps see it.
- `RejectDuplicateOwnerHousehold.java` and `AssignOwnerHousehold.java` — address comparisons (household duplicate detection and the shared `householdId` derivation) now canonicalize both sides via `AddressNormalizer.normalize`, replacing the old lowercase-only rule. Last-name comparison is unchanged. Javadocs updated to match.

**Behaviour change:** the required-field check now rejects an address that is blank after normalization (400), and all address comparisons use the normalized form — exactly matching the new acceptance tests (`coreNormalizesWhitespaceAndCase`, `functionalityExpandsAbbreviations`, `errorRejectsBlankAfterNormalize`). Normalization is applied only on create (POST), not on update (PUT), per the spec. Existing controller/repository tests that don't assert the echoed address value remain green.
